problem: Existing lifelong navigation (LN) benchmarks and methods assume a stationary environment across stages, so methods that fuse old and new observations into persistent scene representations are never tested against between-stage scene changes caused by human activity.
motivation: In real LN deployments humans rearrange rooms while the robot is elsewhere, so stored experience is useful but can become stale and misleading. Static benchmarks hide this failure mode, and re-exploring from scratch wastes the reusable parts of prior experience since changes are usually local.
key_idea: EvoNav-Bench extends GOAT-style multi-stage ObjectNav in ProcTHOR with hidden, probabilistic, local between-stage object relocations, and uses it to benchmark scene-representation-reusing agents and simple update heuristics.
insight: Reusing retained object entries helps in fixed scenes but hurts after evolution. In the controlled Fixed/Not Fixed analysis, entry-retaining methods drop significantly while Stage-Reset drops only 2.2% SR. Target verification (MSGNav) and reactive entry correction (FTU) reduce the drop, so staleness handling is the key problem. Perception error can outweigh evolution: under predicted perception, MSGNav, which is designed for perception error, is best, and the heuristics fall below their GT performance.
method: Task formulation: each task has 3-5 ObjectNav stages in one unseen ProcTHOR house, each with its own step budget. Goals are given by category, adjacent objects, appearance description and an image. Objects may be relocated between stages without informing the agent, and the scene is static within a stage.

Evolution scheduling: evolution triggers with p=0.5 per transition. The room is sampled proportionally to assets x visited-factor (3) x not-transition-room x recent-evolved-factor (0.5), using a shortest-path reference trajectory. This implements locality, experience relevance, observability, and post-evolution validity, checked with the AI2-THOR shortest-path planner.

Room modification: SALIENT_OBJECT (p=0.5, moves one large object with the objects on it), RETAIN_GROUP (p=0.4, moves all objects while keeping asset groups) and FULL_SHUFFLE (p=0.1, moves all objects independently). ProcTHOR placement guarantees navigability.

Goal sampling: target scores of 2/1.5/1 by uniqueness, room weights x9 if the room was modified and x0.2 if it was the previous goal room, and moved-object weight x9 for SALIENT_OBJECT. Goals are thus biased toward evolved rooms without always being relocated objects. gpt-4o generates the appearance and unified instructions.

Frontier-Update (FU): keeps ConceptGraph-style object entries and the occupancy map across stages. When new observations contradict the occupancy map, it rebuilds the map, resets the frontiers and abandons the current target. It exposes object-level memory rather than snapshots and pre-ranks the top-5 entries with CLIP before the VLM.

Fail-then-Update (FTU) and Stage-Reset: FTU adds a VLM check on arrival at a stored entry and removes the entry if the target is absent. Stage-Reset clears object entries and the occupancy map at each stage start (search from scratch).
Evaluation protocol: stage-level SR (success radius 2.0 m) and SPL. GT vs Prediction perception settings. Agents carry over their final pose, and the budget resets each stage.

setting.backbone: gpt-4o (frozen) as VLM/LLM in UniGoal, 3D-Mem, MSGNav and the FU/FTU/Stage-Reset heuristics; YOLO-World + SAM + OpenCLIP for prediction perception (UniGoal: Mask R-CNN + Grounded-SAM)
setting.training_data: none (training-free; benchmark also provides a 7,924-task training split, not used)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with camera pose; simulator-provided occupancy map; GT or predicted object masks/semantics
setting.action_space: discrete MoveAhead 0.25 m / Rotate 15° / Stop (UniGoal, 500 actions per stage); target-position selection executed with TeleportFull along planner waypoints (3D-Mem family, 50 decision rounds per stage)
setting.privileged: simulator occupancy map for all methods; GT object masks and semantic labels in the GT setting

numbers_note: Benchmark paper; only the authors' own heuristics are listed as own methods. Baseline numbers (UniGoal, 3D-Mem, MSGNav) are omitted per rules. Controlled Fixed/Not Fixed results are only in a figure (no numbers except Stage-Reset's 2.2% SR drop). Only FU/FTU/Stage-Reset Prediction rows beyond FTU are in Tab. 1 (FU 42.2/32.5, Stage-Reset 46.8/29.6).
results: On the 365-stage test subset, all heuristics beat the evaluated baselines under GT perception. FTU is best (SR 67.4, SPL 53.3 vs MSGNav 59.2/41.3, 3D-Mem 47.7/42.5, UniGoal 20.0/14.9). Under predicted perception MSGNav is best (SR 54.8, SPL 38.2 vs FTU 49.0/35.8). All methods drop on relocated targets.
limitations: Evolution is simulated only as object relocation in ProcTHOR: no insertion/removal, articulated-state changes or human-derived rearrangement patterns, and lower realism than real-world settings.
Evaluation is on a 10% test subset (365 stages) with a single run and gpt-4o-dependent agents, and the simulator occupancy map is provided to all methods.
The heuristics are reactive and sensitive to perception errors, so proactive staleness handling remains open.
